assertions.text: The document makes no claim about Ruth's values or personality that would fit most teachers equally well (for example that she cares about students or wants to make a difference) unless the claim is tied to specific evidence from her material.
assertions.evidence: No generic "cares about students / wants to make a difference" claims appear. Character claims are anchored: "you're unusually good at teaching *adults* how to explain things" (Marcus, Hannah, Kate in MFL, two INSETs); "more follow-through than most" (book in 6 months, 4 years of newsletter).

assertions.text: Each claim the document makes about Ruth's strengths or working patterns names its evidence: a specific project, role, number, or quoted piece of feedback from her material.
assertions.evidence: "Finished: the book (written for named tutees...), the newsletter (1,150 people expecting it, never missed an issue in four years), six summers of marking..., two INSETs (invited by Marcus)"; editor quoted: "Your explanatory writing is genuinely strong, clearer than most of what crosses my desk".

assertions.text: The document names a pattern that distinguishes Ruth's abandoned efforts (the YouTube channel, the tutoring-agency website, the twice-deferred MSc application) from the efforts she finished.
assertions.evidence: Section "The pattern in the abandoned things" lists YouTube, tutoring agency, MSc as abandoned vs book/newsletter/marking/INSETs/mentoring, then: "Every finished thing had a named audience or an external commissioner. Every abandoned thing required you to manufacture demand from strangers before anyone would care."

assertions.text: The document uses her Teachers' Pension figures (the £14,800 a year already accrued, or the roughly £908 a year that each further year of service adds) when weighing any path that involves leaving employed teaching.
assertions.evidence: "You have £14,800 a year accrued, payable from 68. Each further full-time year adds about £908." Applied to exit paths: Path C "your pot freezes at roughly £19,500 at 68... £16,200 a year less than Path B"; Path D "it would cost you the £16,200 a year computed above."

assertions.text: The document states what full-time freelance science writing typically pays and compares that against the income Ruth's outgoings require.
assertions.evidence: Path D gives only a book-advance range ("typically £5,000–£15,000... over more than two years") and a Ruth-specific "£500–£2,000 a year" — no typical annual freelance-writing income, and the rejection is qualitative ("not viable"), never set against the £31,704/yr outgoings.

assertions.text: Ruth's actual submission record (11 pitches, 2 acceptances, £220 earned) is used as evidence when the document assesses her prospects as a writer.
assertions.evidence: Path D: "£220 in two years. Eleven pitches, two accepted... As a sole income before 2036 this is not viable on any evidence in your files." Also "Nine of your eleven rejections were you offering a thing that this market doesn't purchase," feeding the £500–£2,000/yr projection.

assertions.text: Each proposed path is given its own distinct way of failing, different from the failure modes of the other paths.
assertions.evidence: A: "ill-health retirement... arrives when your voice decides"; C: "your pot freezes at roughly £19,500... They don't clear the bar"; D: "No pension, no sick pay... not viable on any evidence"; B: "real surplus is under £200 a month. Then 0.8 in September 2027 is too early" — four distinct failures.

assertions.text: Every proposed path states an observable sign, within a stated time window, that would show the path is not working.
assertions.evidence: Paths A, C, D and E state no failure sign at all — e.g. Path D ends "As a *stream inside* Path B it's already real". "What would change my mind" is plan-level, and its nearest items lack windows ("Two commissions is a signal; one isn't").

assertions.text: At least one option is explicitly ruled out, deferred, or restructured because her £8,412 of savings cover only about three months of outgoings.
assertions.evidence: "Your savings are £8,412, which is 3.2 months of outgoings" → "get the emergency fund to £15,850, six months of outgoings. You're at £8,412... Treat this as the gate on the 0.8 move: hit the number, then reduce." The 0.8 step is deferred until the thin fund is rebuilt.

assertions.text: No recommended step requires Ruth to leave the Sheffield area before Alice finishes school in summer 2029.
assertions.evidence: Every recommended step is Sheffield-based: "0.8 from September 2027" at Ashworth via "a formal flexible working request"; APE is "Twenty days a year, mostly remote"; the timeline holds "2027–29 — 0.8. Alice through GCSEs and A-levels." Path C (exit) is deferred: "a Path B branch for the 2030s, not a 2029 decision."

assertions.text: The document commits to one recommended direction for Ruth, with its reasoning stated, rather than presenting the paths as equally weighted choices for her to pick from.
assertions.evidence: "## The verdict, before the working / Go part-time, in stages, and never leave the Teachers' Pension Scheme." Path B is marked "← recommended"; Paths A/C/D are argued down ("Listed for completeness. I don't recommend it."), with a "Which one, and why" section giving the £16,200/yr pension reasoning.

assertions.text: The document names the conflict between Ruth's statement that she is not a leader and the evidence of her leading in her record (running staff training, leading an exam-marking team of 11, mentoring early-career teachers), rather than silently accepting either side.
assertions.evidence: "What Marcus, Hannah, Kate in MFL and two INSETs are actually describing is that you're unusually good at teaching *adults*... 'I'm not a leader' is probably accurate about the head of department job and probably not accurate as a general claim." — names the conflict, accepts neither side.

assertions.text: The recommended path's first steps are specific enough to begin within a few weeks: a named request, application, message, or task, not an instruction to explore, reflect, or network.
assertions.evidence: "By 26 September 2026 — apply for Assistant Principal Examiner"; "This month — see your GP again and ask for an occupational health referral, and an ENT or speech-and-language therapy referral"; "September or October 2026 — submit a formal flexible working request for 0.8 from September 2027".

assertions.text: The document names external events (in her school, the exam system, her finances, or Alice's plans) that should cause the plan to be re-examined.
assertions.evidence: "What would change my mind" lists external triggers: "The exam board says APE conflicts with the book line"; "A school-based or scheme-eligible teacher-training role appears"; "A publisher approaches you about the newsletter or the books"; "The spending tracking shows the real surplus is under £200 a month."
